clue.text: Exempting king from compulsory recruitment is silly

indicators.note: exempting the king means letting him off, so his letter is excused from the word

parts.note: the draft is conscription into the armed forces
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: Someone argues that letting a monarch off national service would be a foolish idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exempting' tells you to drop the king's letter R from DRAFT.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal synonyms for foolish or lacking sense.

clue.text: Kill a proportion of rodents turning up in tree

indicators.note: in places the turned word for rodents inside the tree

parts.note: a date is a palm tree

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means read from bottom to top, so the word is reversed

parts.note: mice are small rodents

explanation.surface: Rodents scurrying up a tree are culled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' gives ECIM. The Roman army once executed one soldier in every ten, which is why killing a proportion defines the word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word originally meant to execute one in ten, so destroying a part of a group fits.

clue.text: Final manuscript of Oberon, perhaps showing input of constant work

indicators.note: input of means the following letters are put into the word for Oberon

parts.note: Oberon is king of the fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream, so an example of a fairy
C is the symbol for a constant, as for the speed of light
OP, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare scholar's final draft about the fairy king shows steady work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing' is only a link. Oberon is the fairy king in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: A neat, corrected version of a document made after drafting is the finished manuscript.

clue.text: Settle area after re-building property

indicators.note: re-building means constructing again in a new form, so these ten letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A developer agrees to settle a district once reconstruction is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is a link: 'Settle' looks like a verb with 'area' its object, but both words are just raw letters for 're-building'.
explanation.definitionFit: Land and buildings held as assets are known collectively by this phrase, a synonym for property.

clue.text: Weariness is genuine — endlessly shattered

indicators.note: shattered means broken into pieces, so the letters are rearranged
endlessly means the first and last letters are removed

explanation.surface: Someone's exhaustion is real, broken without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' leaves ENUIN, which 'shattered' rearranges. 'Shattered' is also British slang for exhausted, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a feeling of listless boredom and tiredness, a synonym for weariness.

clue.text: Painting places and characters in a new setting

indicators.note: the characters, or letters, are placed in a new order

explanation.surface: An artist moves locations and figures into a fresh setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters in a new setting' rearranges the letters of PLACES AND.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture of countryside scenery is a kind of painting.

clue.text: Wills place once — or wells place?

explanation.definitionFit: A London building that once held the national registry of wills; also any house in the county containing the city of Wells.

clue.text: Rising of the sun has daughter missing sunshade

indicators.note: missing means the letter for daughter is left out of the word

parts.note: dawning is the coming of daylight, the sun rising

explanation.surface: A family scene: at sunrise the daughter forgets the parasol.
explanation.walkthrough: DAWNING loses its D; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvas sheet stretched over a window or shop front shades it from the sun.

clue.text: Invest millions in river port free from tax, say

indicators.note: invest X in Y means X is put inside Y, so the letter goes into the river and port

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, in south-west England
PT is an abbreviation for port, as in place names
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Someone puts millions into a Devon harbour town and claims tax relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invest ... in' is the container signal: putting millions into something sounds financial, but here the letter for millions simply goes inside. The Exe is a river in Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: Being excused from a duty, such as paying tax, is one example of the sense; hence 'say'.

clue.text: Such fabric is unsatisfactory when spun in much of eastern country

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the shortened country name
much of means not quite all, so the country loses its last letter

parts.note: China is a country in East Asia

indicators.note: spun means turned round, so the word for unsatisfactory is read backwards

parts.note: off, as of food or a performance, means not up to standard

explanation.surface: A complaint that a sheer fabric made in the Far East goes bad in the spin cycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when spun' gives FFO, and 'much of' trims the country to CHIN.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a light, sheer silk or nylon material, so it is one kind of fabric.

clue.text: Achievement finding some cattle left out in northern Ireland brush

parts.note: a feat is an achievement
a herd is a group of cattle

indicators.note: out in means the letter for left is removed from the province's name

parts.note: Ulster is the northern province of Ireland, often used for Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A farming success story: some cattle left loose in Ulster.
explanation.walkthrough: FEAT + HERD + ULSTER without its L ('out in'), leaving USTER; 'finding' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a cleaning tool, a stick tipped with plumes for flicking away dust, so a brush.

clue.text: No real owner of old pit in Tyneside?

indicators.note: in puts the old pit inside the letters for the region

parts.note: Tyneside, around Newcastle, is in the North East of England, NE
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A question whether the old Tyneside colliery actually belongs to anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside, around Newcastle in North East England, was once a great coal-mining area, so the surface reads naturally; 'No' belongs to the definition, not the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who holds shares or property in name only, on behalf of the real beneficiary, is not the true owner.

clue.text: Branch of applied science that's changed since Mach

indicators.note: changed means altered in form, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A claim that physics has moved on since Ernst Mach, the physicist of the Mach number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges SINCE MACH; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The study of forces and motion, and its use in machines, is a field of applied science.

clue.text: Bowler's approach brought back humour to game

indicators.note: humour to game means the turned word is attached after the letters for the game

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game

indicators.note: brought back means returned, so the word for humour is read backwards

parts.note: a pun is a joke based on wordplay, a piece of humour

explanation.surface: A sports report says wit was restored to a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' gives NUP. In cricket the bowler runs in towards the stumps before delivering the ball; the game here is rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, the run a bowler takes before releasing the ball is called this.

clue.text: One point he's caught in stories to make all the difference

indicators.note: in places the run of small pieces inside the word for stories

parts.note: tales are stories
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written without the apostrophe
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A storyteller notes that one detail of someone being caught can change everything.
explanation.walkthrough: The small pieces sit inside the stories just after their first letter. 'make all the difference' is the definition, a verb phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To be the deciding factor, tilting a balance one way, is an idiom for being decisive.

clue.text: Railway worker striking over lots being cut

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the first word above the second

parts.note: signal, as an adjective, means notable or striking

indicators.note: being cut means the word for lots loses its last letter

parts.note: many means lots

explanation.surface: A railway employee on strike over many redundancies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being cut' drops the last letter of the word for lots. 'striking' looks like industrial action but is the adjective meaning notable.
explanation.definitionFit: He operates the signals on a railway line, so he is a rail employee.

clue.text: Painkiller I had injected into traumatised pleura

indicators.note: injected into means the contracted pronoun and verb are put inside the other letters
traumatised means badly shaken, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A patient was given pain relief by injection into an injured lung lining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traumatised' gives EPURAL, and 'injected into' splits it after EP. The pleura is the membrane round the lungs.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an anaesthetic injected near the spine, often in childbirth, to block pain.

clue.text: Made a serious error reportedly over church collection of twenty four's

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the first part above the second
reportedly means the word is as heard, so its sound is spelt differently

parts.note: sinned means committed a wrong, a serious error
Rome stands for the Roman Catholic Church

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to a grave mistake over a church collection.
explanation.walkthrough: SINNED, said aloud, gives SYND, over ROME. The definition refers to 24 across, signs that all is not well: a set of them is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of signs that together mark a medical condition is the meaning; 24 across gives the single sign.

clue.text: Ready to fire scaffolding worker mildly drunk after a short time

indicators.note: after says the worker and the tipsy word come behind the letter for time

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, the word shortened
a rigger erects scaffolding or ship's rigging
happy is a jokey term for slightly tipsy

explanation.surface: A building-site worker gets tipsy after only a few minutes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a short time' is time cut to its abbreviation. A rigger erects scaffolding on building sites.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes someone too eager to shoot, which is being over-ready to fire a gun.

clue.text: Rock group may initially fool one beginning to film

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of the word

parts.note: an ass is a fool
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A rock band might at first fool someone starting out in film.
explanation.walkthrough: M + ASS + I + F.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a compact group of mountains, a mass of rock forming a range.

clue.text: Ford becomes formal only if this is so pitifully bad

parts.words: Ford becomes formal only if this is so
parts.note: the word Ford turns into formal only when its last letter is replaced by three others, a statement the answer split into three words makes

explanation.surface: A car maker's mark goes upmarket only on a condition.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as D IS MAL: when D becomes MAL, Ford becomes FORMAL.
explanation.definitionFit: It means gloomy and miserable, or of very poor quality, close to pitifully bad.

clue.text: Cease to live in a university — goodbye!

indicators.note: in places the word for dying inside the other two letters

parts.note: to cease to live is to die

explanation.surface: A grim farewell from someone who expects to end their days at college.
explanation.walkthrough: DIE goes inside A and U.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a French farewell, used in English as a synonym for farewell.

clue.text: Amazed concerning vampires: perhaps there is no answer

parts.note: as to means concerning or about

indicators.note: there is no means the letter for answer is missing from the word

parts.note: vampires are an example of the undead, the walking dead of horror stories

explanation.surface: Someone stunned to find no explanation for vampires.
explanation.walkthrough: AS TO is followed by UNDEAD with its A removed by 'there is no', leaving UNDED.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe being overcome with surprise, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Tax increasing the holy exchequer, primarily

definitions.text: Tax increasing the holy exchequer, primarily

indicators.note: primarily means take the first letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: A levy that swells the church's coffers.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of Tax Increasing The Holy Exchequer spell the answer, and the whole clue defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: It was a church levy of one tenth of produce or income, swelling holy funds.

clue.text: Prissy MP to marry, concealing sign all's not well

indicators.note: concealing means the answer sits inside the run of words that come before it

explanation.surface: A prim politician is about to wed, which hides a warning sign of trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run through prisSY MP TO Marry.
explanation.definitionFit: A symptom is an indication of illness or of a deeper problem.

clue.text: One played lead in Othello at the globe

parts.note: an orb is a globe, so the globe gives the orb

indicators.note: lead in means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone took the leading role in a Shakespeare tragedy at the Globe theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: THE ORB is followed by O, the first letter of Othello; 'at' is a link. The Globe is Shakespeare's London theatre, but here it is just an orb. A theorbo is a large lute.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a large bass lute of the 17th century, a musical instrument, so something one plays.

clue.text: One roaming moors gave into temptation to shoot

parts.note: fell, as in fell from grace, means yielded to temptation
a runner is a creeping shoot of a plant such as a strawberry

explanation.surface: Someone yielded to the urge to go shooting on the grouse moors.
explanation.walkthrough: A fell is also a hill in northern England, which helps the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who races over hills and moorland on foot covers open upland country.

clue.text: Stick with black for good colour

indicators.note: black for good means the letter for black replaces the letter for good

parts.note: glue is an adhesive that sticks things
B is the pencil abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: An instruction to stay with black as a permanent colour choice.
explanation.walkthrough: In GLUE, B replaces G; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the colour of a clear sky, one of the primary colours.
